result.verifier:
Check out the pull request head for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 and run every command from the repository root. Each check below matches one expect line, in order.

Check 1 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before"
Run:
`d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n' > $d/a.jsonl && printf '{"ok":1}\n' > $d/b.jsonl && printf 'x\n\n{"c":' > $d/c.jsonl && node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/a.jsonl $d/b.jsonl $d/c.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"; for f in a c; do node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/$f.jsonl; done`
PASS: the multi-file run prints the a.jsonl line(s) (`<dir>/a.jsonl:2: <error>`) followed by the c.jsonl lines (`<dir>/c.jsonl:1: ...` and `<dir>/c.jsonl:3: ...`), nothing for b.jsonl, and those lines equal the concatenation of the two single-file runs' output in argument order.
FAIL: any file is skipped, lines are out of argument order, a clean file produces output, or a line differs from the single-file `<file>:<line>: <error>` format.

Check 2 — expect: "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)"
Run: `printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js -; echo "exit=$?"` and `printf '{"a":1}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js - -; echo "exit=$?"`
PASS: the first prints a line starting `-:2: ` (stdin was read and reported as `-`); the second exits 2.
FAIL: stdin is not read, it is reported under another name, or two `-` arguments do not exit 2.

Check 3 — expect: "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)"
Run:
`d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '{"a":1}\n' > $d/ok1.jsonl && printf '[1]\n' > $d/ok2.jsonl && printf '{bad}\n' > $d/bad.jsonl && J=packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js; node $J $d/ok1.jsonl $d/ok2.jsonl; echo "clean exit=$?"; node $J $d/ok1.jsonl $d/bad.jsonl $d/ok2.jsonl; echo "bad exit=$?"; node $J; echo "none exit=$?"; node $J $d/ok1.jsonl $d/missing.jsonl $d/bad.jsonl 2>$d/err; echo "missing exit=$?"; cat $d/err`
PASS: clean exit=0; bad exit=1; none exit=2 with a message on stderr; missing exit=2, stderr mentions missing.jsonl, and stdout still includes the `<dir>/bad.jsonl:1: ` line (the other files were checked and reported).
FAIL: any of those exit codes differ, the missing-file error is not on stderr, or bad.jsonl's row is not reported in the missing-file run.

Check 4 — expect: "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged"
Run: `git fetch origin main && git diff origin/main...HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`
PASS: the diff is empty.
FAIL: the diff shows any change to the lint function (a change to anything else in that file is also suspicious; report it).

Check 5 — expect: "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage"
Run: `(cd packages/jsonl-lint && node --test)` and read packages/jsonl-lint/test/*.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md at the head.
PASS: node:test tests exist that cover each of: two clean files; one bad file among several; stdin via `-` clean; stdin via `-` bad; a missing file among good ones; two `-` arguments; no arguments — and the README documents the multi-file usage (`<file> [<file> ...]`) and `-` for stdin.
FAIL: any of those seven cases has no test, or the README does not document the usage.

Check 6 — expect: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run: `npm ci && npm test; echo "exit=$?"`, then `gh pr view <PR number> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid,state` and `gh pr checks <PR number> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test`.
PASS: it is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test, its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, `npm test` passes, and the `test` workflow check at the head commit is green.
FAIL: the body lacks that text, npm test fails, or the test workflow check at the head is failing or missing.

Advisory (not pass/fail):
- Usage/stderr wording, exact error text and whether a usage message is printed for two `-` are free choices.
- Nice to have: the missing-file error message format `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: ...` matches the old one; existing single-file tests still pass unchanged.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #104 and the harness accepted them. I didn't change, commit or push anything.

**Builder brief:** It covers three files: the CLI script, its test file and the package README. `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` must not be touched.
- **CLI:** `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` takes several files and checks them in the order given. Output for each file stays exactly as it is now for a single file.
- **Stdin:** `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`. A second `-` is a usage error that exits 2 before anything is read.
- **Unreadable files:** if a file can't be read, the error goes to stderr and the other files are still checked. The run then exits 2. Otherwise it exits 1 if any row is bad and 0 if every file is clean.
- **Tests and README:** `node:test` tests are added for each case the issue lists, and the README is updated with the new usage and exit codes. Then `npm test` must pass, and one PR is opened whose body contains the `Closes …/issues/104` line.

**Verifier brief:** It has six checks, one per acceptance line and in the same order. Each one runs commands at the PR head:
1. It runs the CLI on several files and compares the output with single-file runs, in argument order.
2. It pipes rows into `-`, and runs `- -` to confirm it exits 2.
3. It checks each exit code (0, 1 and 2), including a missing file among good ones. The bad file's rows must still be reported in that run.
4. It diffs `packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` against `origin/main`, and the diff must be empty.
5. It runs the package tests and reads the tests and README to confirm all seven required cases are covered and the usage is documented.
6. It runs `npm ci && npm test`, reads the PR body for the `Closes` line, and confirms the `test` workflow check is green at the head.

Stricter details that the acceptance lines don't name are listed under "Advisory" and are not pass/fail conditions. These include the usage and error wording, and keeping the old "cannot read" message format.

The issue gave no proofs, so I chose a check for each line myself.
